hypothesis: HYPE breakout-onset entries whose completed five-minute breakout direction agrees with the completed-hour structural direction may outperform entries where those directions oppose after live costs.
decision: Reject adding a five-minute direction agreement gate or replacing the completed-hour structural entry side. Retain the current structural direction contract and continue collecting exact breakout-side relation telemetry without changing, gating, closing, or resizing live execution.
falsifier: Reconsider only if a causal live sample with exact breakout-side relation coverage shows aligned entries materially outperforming opposed entries after fees, funding, and slippage, and a purged out-of-sample challenger using the active 8-to-24-hour lifecycle contract outperforms the structural-side baseline on net return and drawdown.
limitations: Only four of seven closed live HYPE trades have attributable component stance, and only one is aligned.
The seven legacy closes lack exact breakout-side relation telemetry, so component stance is descriptive rather than a substitute label.
The 365-day venue-matched challenger uses one-minute bars, fixed slippage, an 80-bps stop, and a fixed eight-hour hold rather than the active soft-eight-to-hard-twenty-four-hour lifecycle.
Both offline direction variants lost after modeled friction, so their relative ranking does not establish standalone edge.
The currently open opposed HYPE lifecycle is excluded until its outcome resolves.
